tagline: An original Pokemon-style overworld, collectible evolving Guardians, real-world family missions, and a village that visibly grows. Built against the FireRed/LeafGreen and Littlewood quality bar, and verified by driving the real game rather than reading its code.

pieces.note: 60Hz fixed step, layered pixel renderer, input, scenes, procedural audio, save, pixel font, hook bridge

pieces.name: Art system
pieces.note: 420 sprites. Grass retextured; each Guardian archetype now has its own proportions rather than one shared egg

pieces.note: 5 connected maps + 3 interiors, tap-turn/hold-walk movement, NPCs, day/night/seasons, encounters

findings.title: The village paved everything it could see
findings.detail: Ground finishing at level 6 had a radius wider than the screen, and its outer band used near-white stones on dark grey in cold tones beside a warm sand plaza — it read as a missing-texture checkerboard. Radius cut below screen width, paving warmed and its value gap closed, and the outer fifth now dissolves into grass instead of stopping at a hard ring.

findings.title: Night light was applied in the wrong order
findings.detail: Additive lamp glow ran before the darkening tint, so it saturated bright tiles to white before the tint could touch them. Darken first, then punch light through — and pool it on the ground below a lamp rather than on the fitting.

findings.title: The game was completely silent
findings.detail: The sfx kit existed but no songs had ever been written. Nine original songs now cover every map and scene, and the regression asserts both that they exist and that the sequencer runs real ticks without throwing.

findings.title: All five builder subagents were killed mid-flight
findings.detail: The account hit its monthly spend limit, terminating every parallel builder. Their partial output was salvaged, verified, and completed directly in the main session.

findings.title: Every Guardian shares one egg silhouette
findings.detail: Six body archetypes now change the actual proportions — squat Terranox, upright birds with a visible chest, legless tapering wisps, wide quadrupeds, small sprites, upright drakes.

findings.title: Brow shadow read as spectacles
findings.detail: An early pass at more expressive faces put a dark bar above the eyes that looked like glasses on half the roster. Removed.

findings.title: Type badges were anonymous colour blocks
findings.detail: A coloured rectangle tells the player nothing. Badges now carry their type name.

findings.title: Player HP readout collided with its panel edge
findings.detail: Found by looking at the capture, not the code. Panel re-laid out with the XP bar labelled.

findings.title: Entering build mode directly threw
findings.detail: With no building type the placement validator crashed, and because the first scene was entered before the test API was exposed, that failure blanked the whole harness instead of reporting itself. Both fixed.

findings.title: Locked rows said 'locked' and nothing else
findings.detail: The model had a reason string all along; the UI was reading the wrong field. Rows now say Needs Village Level 3, or which mission opens them.

findings.title: Benefit text spilled off the panel
findings.detail: Now wrapped and clipped to the panel bounds.

findings.title: Header and tabs collided at fixed spacing
findings.detail: 'In Emberhollow' overran 'Done'. Both rows are now measured, not evenly spaced.

findings.title: The boot veil bled into every screenshot
findings.detail: Captures fired during the 450ms fade, so the loading text sat over the game in every image. The veil now leaves the compositor, and the harness retires it outright.

findings.title: Grass reads as a flat green plane
findings.detail: Rewritten with 2x2 block mottling plus five blade tufts per tile. A first pass overshot into gravel-looking static with more internal contrast than the path, so it was dialled back: walkable ground must stay calmer than what stands on it.

findings.title: Dialogue still runs on the foundation fallback
findings.detail: It works and it wraps correctly, but it has no portraits, no speed control, and no designed frame. The dedicated textbox was one of the builders that was cut off.

findings.title: Faces are still one arrangement across the roster
findings.detail: Two dots and a nose on every species. Now that silhouettes differ, per-archetype eye shapes and mouths are the next gain.

findings.title: Some evolutions are too close in colour
findings.detail: Aquarabbit and Torrentide read as the same blue at a glance; the mass change carries the evolution but the palette does not help.

findings.title: Night lamps read as pale signboards
findings.detail: Three wrong diagnoses before the right one: not the glow, not a fallback painter, not the lighting order. Rendering the tile on its own at 8x settled it — a wide rectangular head on a thin post reads as a signboard, and at night the bright pane made it a white block. Redrawn as a lantern: tapered body, peaked cap, a mullion and cross-bar splitting the glass into panes, hooked arm, footed post.

comparisons.title: The same ground at village level 1 and level 6

a.label: level 1 — the Hearthstone and not much else

b.label: level 6 — eleven buildings at top tier

comparisons.verdict: The transformation is unmistakable: paved plaza, banners, lamps, benches, planters, a market stall, and villagers who moved in. Running this pair is also what exposed the paving defect — the first version covered every tile in view.

timeline.label: Foundation landed
timeline.detail: Zero-build ES-module engine: 60Hz fixed timestep, 320x180 layered renderer with y-sorted entities, edge-buffered input across keyboard/gamepad/touch, scene stack, procedural audio sequencer, save with migrations, hand-built pixel font.

timeline.label: Contracts pinned
timeline.detail: CONTRACTS.md fixed ownership and the quality bar; art/names.js pinned all 413 sprite names, the 18-Guardian roster, the cast, and building footprints; core/bridge.js gave every cross-piece call a late-bound safe default.

timeline.label: Five builders fanned out
timeline.detail: Art, overworld, battle, village+missions, and UI each handed to a fresh-context builder with disjoint file ownership.

timeline.label: All five builders killed
timeline.detail: The account hit its monthly spend limit and every parallel builder terminated mid-task. Their partial output — tiles, sprites, the battle engine, species, moves, missions, the village model, UI frames — was salvaged, syntax-verified, and committed.

timeline.label: Overworld built
timeline.detail: The critical gap: there was no game to play. Five connected maps plus three interiors, authored with a small DSL; autotiled shorelines and paths; 2x2 tree canopies the player walks behind; movement where a tap turns and a hold walks and steps never stutter.

timeline.label: Art completed
timeline.detail: 18 Guardians from one parametric painter so the roster reads as a family and evolutions read as growth; the full effects kit; UI chrome. All 413 required sprites present.

timeline.label: Battle scene built
timeline.detail: The engine's event stream turned into presentation: draining bars, hit flashes, shake scaled to effectiveness, an arcing charm for bonding, an evolution overlay.

timeline.label: Village, missions, and the front end
timeline.detail: Build board, ghost placement, before/after upgrade card, the mission corkboard, title, pause, party, summary, and records.

timeline.label: Whole-experience pass green
timeline.detail: 27/27 checks: every scene reachable and rendering, no console errors, movement and save verified, 60fps. Nine defects found by looking at real captures rather than reading code.

timeline.label: Grass, silhouettes, and a score
timeline.detail: Closed the two biggest open findings: the flat grass plane and the shared Guardian silhouette. Wrote the game's music from scratch — it had been entirely silent. Regression grew to 29 checks.

timeline.label: The village earns its claim
timeline.detail: Built an A/B that takes the same ground from level 1 to level 6 and shoots both from the same camera. The transformation is unmistakable — and running it caught the village paving every visible tile in a cold grey checkerboard, plus night light being composited in the wrong order.

timeline.label: The lamp, correctly diagnosed
timeline.detail: Closed the defect left open last cycle. The useful part was being wrong three times: each failed fix ruled out a cause, and rendering the tile alone at 8x on grass showed the real problem was the silhouette, not the lighting.
